drill_stem_test_results:
A single drill stem test of the fulmar sands was devised to be run in two parts. Due to the lower than expected permeability of the upper sand members an initial test was carried out on this sand DST1 and then the main high permeability sands perforated and tested as DST 2 without pulling the test string. 

DST-1 - The formation did not flow at measurable productive rates , however some fluid was recovered into the gauge tank. detailed examination of the downhaul shut in and flow periods of DST one show that the formation was open but the flow capacity was very low with either sea water or Base Oil as the cushion. An unsuccessful attempt was made to induce flow pressure by pulsing. The formations have possibly been heavily damaged by the drilling fluid but do show that fluid movement is possible .

DST-2  - was perforated with 600 PSI underbalanced using the TCP guns and gave immediate pressure response at the surface. The formation flowed freely but did not establish stabilised conditions at the end of the main flow. 

A discontinuity probably a fault is identifiable from the buildup analysis approximately 200 feet from the wellbore. The test results do not give any clear indication of the reservoir size or extent but do indicate a constraint to well and formation productivity. 

The formations may be heterogeneous however this is not absolute clear from these tests. The cause indicates formations with very good permeability yet there is apparent restriction to flow in the reservoir. The formations have 375md average permeability. A negative skin factor of -2.6 has been calculated based on a well bore diameter 6,25 inches and a production index of 2.2 bbls/PSI measured in the final flow. 

Conclusions 
1 - The test is a valid test recovering representative fluid samples and pressure data 
2 - The reservoir is heterogeneous and will need careful further evaluation 
3 - The low oil gravity and GOR reduced the overall well production performance 
4 - The apparent reservoir pressure depletion whilst testing is not conclusive evidence of a very limited reservoir. It may be due in part to restricted formation productivity away from the wellbore 
5 - There was no identifiable evidence that a reservoir limit was seen during this test

reservoir_description:
E&A wells demonstrate excellent quality reservoir which correlates across the accumulation, with a stratigraphic division observed
Upper, ratty injected sand ‘halo’ unit (8-25ft thick) occurring above E&A wells, generally absent in offsets.  Characterised by complex, high-angle & unpredictable sand geometries•Lower, blocky ‘massive sand’ unit (56-80ft thick inside Fotla field, up to 133ft in 8 well –channel axis?)
Static parameters in-line with pre-drill expectations from offset wells: high quality, high poroperm & mobility (>30% ?& D-scale K), high oil saturations (~85%)
Alternative working geological interpretations for depositional origin: highly remobilised deep marine channel complex, sandstone injectite complex or hybrid injectite/ remobilised channel system.  Further work to address uncertainty in depositional origin ongoing (e.g. HM studies), alternative realisations to be captured in post-well work
connectivity: During the Fotla E&A programme, successful pressure and sampling activities have been undertaken on all three wells, which have supported characterisation of a common fluid type across the Fotla field.
